p.src: The tale tells how Lin Chong, the Panther Head, had fallen drunk in the snow that night and could not struggle to his feet. The manor servants bound him and escorted him to a country estate. A servant came out of the compound and said, “The master has not risen yet. For now, string this rogue up beneath the gatehouse.” As dawn approached, Lin Chong awoke from his drunken stupor. Looking about, he saw that it was indeed a splendid great estate. Lin Chong shouted, “Who dares hang me up here?” Hearing him shout, a servant came through the gate with a whitewood staff in his hand and barked, “You rogue, you still have the gall to talk so boldly!” The old servant whose beard and whiskers had been singed said, “Do not question him—just beat him! When the master rises, we shall question him properly and turn him over to the authorities.” The servants rushed him together. Unable to resist their blows, Lin Chong could only cry, “Do not beat me! I can explain myself.” Just then another servant came and called, “The master is here.” Lin Chong looked and saw a gentleman walking out with his hands clasped behind his back. Reaching the veranda, he asked, “Whom are you beating here?” The servants answered, “We caught a rice thief last night.” The gentleman stepped forward to look and recognized Lin Chong. Hastily ordering the servants back, he personally cut him down and asked, “Instructor, how did you come to be hanging here?” At the sight of this, all the servants slipped away.

p.src: When Lin Chong looked, he saw none other than Chai Jin, the Little Whirlwind, and promptly cried, “Master, save me!” Chai Jin said, “Instructor, how did you come here and suffer such humiliation at the hands of these country bumpkins?” Lin Chong replied, “It is a long story!” The two went inside and sat down, whereupon Lin Chong related in full the affair of the burning fodder depot. When Chai Jin had heard him out, he said, “Brother, how cruelly fortune has thwarted you! Today Heaven has granted us this fortunate chance, so set your mind at ease. This is my eastern estate. Stay here for a while, and afterward we shall decide what to do.” He ordered a servant to bring out a chest of clothes and had Lin Chong change everything he wore, from his innermost garments outward. He invited him to sit in a warm chamber and had wine, food, cups, and dishes prepared to entertain him. From then on, Lin Chong stayed five or seven days at Chai Jin’s eastern estate. Of this no more need be said.

p.src: Meanwhile, the commandant of the Cangzhou prison camp formally reported that Lin Chong had killed three men—the assignment officer, Lieutenant Lu, and Fu An—and had set fire to the army fodder depot, causing the blaze to spread. The prefect was greatly alarmed. He immediately issued official warrants, commanding the arrest officers to take constables through every village and district, along roads, at inns, and in rural settlements. Notices were posted everywhere, offering a reward of three thousand strings of cash for the capture of the principal culprit, Lin Chong. Before long the pursuit grew intense, and every village and settlement was astir with the news.

p.src: Lin Chong said, “If you would support me in this way, sir, and give me a place where I may establish myself, I only wonder where I am to go?” Chai Jin replied, “In Jizhou Prefecture, Shandong, there is a region of lakes and marshes called Liangshan Marsh. It extends more than eight hundred li around, and at its heart lie Wanzi Stockade and Liao’er Hollow. At present three gallant men have established a stronghold there. Their leader is Wang Lun, called the White-Robed Scholar; the second is Du Qian, called Touching the Sky; and the third is Song Wan, called Guardian King in the Clouds. Those three heroes have gathered seven or eight hundred lesser bandits and raid homes and plunder travelers. Many who have committed crimes so great as to affront Heaven flee there to escape disaster, and the three take them all in. The three heroes are also close friends of mine and have often sent me letters. I shall now write you a letter, brother. How would it be for you to go there and join their band?” Lin Chong said, “If you would show me such consideration, nothing could be better!” Chai Jin said, “There is only this difficulty: the authorities have posted warrants at the Cangzhou checkpoint and assigned two officers to inspect travelers and guard the pass. You must pass that way, brother.” Chai Jin lowered his head in thought, then said, “I have another plan to get you safely through.” Lin Chong said, “If you can see me safely through, I shall not forget it even in death.”

p.src: That same day, Chai Jin first ordered a servant to carry Lin Chong’s bundle through the pass and wait outside. Chai Jin then readied twenty or thirty horses, took bows, arrows, flags, and spears, mounted hawks and eagles on perches, and leashed hunting dogs. When the whole company was equipped, he mingled Lin Chong among them. They all mounted and headed outside the pass. Now the officers guarding the pass were seated above the gate. When they saw that it was Master Chai, they recognized him at once. It happened that before inheriting his post, one of these officers had visited Chai Jin’s estate, and so they knew each other well. The officer rose and said, “Off for more sport, Master?” Chai Jin dismounted and asked, “What brings you two gentlemen here?” The officer replied, “The prefect of Cangzhou has circulated official orders, complete with a portrait and description, for the arrest of the criminal Lin Chong. We have been specially assigned to guard this place. Every passing traveler or merchant must be questioned one by one before being allowed through the pass.” Chai Jin laughed and said, “I have Lin Chong hidden among this company of mine. How is it that you do not recognize him?” The officer laughed too. “You are a man who knows the law, Master. Surely you would never smuggle him through? Please mount and go as you please.” Chai Jin laughed again. “Then I entrust the matter to you. When I bring down some game, I shall send you a share.” After taking their leave, they all mounted and rode through the pass.

p.src: After traveling fourteen or fifteen li, they found the servant who had gone ahead waiting there. Chai Jin had Lin Chong dismount and take off his hunting clothes. Lin Chong put on his own garments, which the servant had brought, fastened a saber at his waist, donned a felt hat with a red tassel, shouldered his bundle, and took up his broad-bladed sword. Then he bade Chai Jin farewell, bowed in parting, and set off. As for Chai Jin and his company, they mounted and went hunting. They did not return until evening, when they passed through the checkpoint as before, gave the officers some game, and returned to the estate. Of this no more need be said.

p.src: The heavenly powers rage, overturning the silver sea and scattering its beaded curtains. Six-petalled wondrous blossoms whirl through the air, leveling the hills and ravines among the mountains. White tigers run mad, pale qilins rampage, snapping their strings of pearls. Jade dragons battle furiously, their scales and armor falling across the sky. Who thinks of the frontier passes ten thousand miles away, where soldiers stand frozen and white streamers cling wetly to the feet of their banners? Its hue gleams upon spears, its light dances over swords and halberds, while the air of slaughter spreads across the army tents. Tiger-bold heroes and valiant officers gather to discuss the arts of war. Come, let us drink ourselves insensible and gaze upon the vast blue sky.

p.src: At the sight, Lin Chong hurried into the inn. He raised the reed curtain, brushed the snow from himself, and stepped inside. Looking about, he saw tables and benches everywhere. He chose a place to sit, leaned his long sword against it, untied his bundle, removed his felt hat, and hung up the saber at his waist. A waiter came over and asked, “How much wine would you like, sir?” “Bring me two horns to begin with,” said Lin Chong. The waiter drew two horns of wine into a small vessel, brought it over, and set it on the table. Lin Chong then asked, “What have you to eat with the wine?” “Raw and cooked beef, fat goose, and tender chicken,” replied the waiter. “First cut me two catties of cooked beef,” said Lin Chong. Before long the waiter returned, laid out a large platter of beef and several dishes of vegetables, set down a large bowl, and began pouring the wine. After Lin Chong had drunk three or four bowls, a man from within the inn emerged with his hands clasped behind his back and went to the doorway to watch the snow. The man asked the waiter, “Who is drinking there?” Lin Chong looked at him. He wore a warm hat with a deep brim, a marten-fur coat, and close-fitting boots of roebuck hide. He was tall and powerfully built, with a broad, formidable face, prominent cheekbones, and a three-pronged yellow beard. He merely stroked his head as he watched the snow. Lin Chong told the waiter to keep pouring. Then he said, “Waiter, come have a bowl yourself.” The waiter drank a bowl. Lin Chong asked, “How far is it from here to Liangshan Marsh?” The waiter replied, “Liangshan Marsh is only a few li from here, but the way is entirely by water; there is no road overland. If you wish to go, you must take a boat; only then can you cross to the place.” “Then find me a boat,” said Lin Chong. The waiter said, “In such heavy snow, and with night already falling, where could I find a boat?” “I will pay you extra,” said Lin Chong. “Please find a boat and ferry me across.” “There is simply nowhere to obtain one,” replied the waiter. Lin Chong thought, “What am I to do now?” He drank several more bowls, and gloom rose in his heart. Suddenly he thought, “Once I was an arms instructor in the capital, roaming its bustling streets and markets every day, drinking and taking my ease. Who would have imagined that the villain Gao Qiu would ensnare me so cruelly, have my face branded, and drive me all the way here, leaving me unable to return to my home or seek refuge in my country, condemned to endure this loneliness!” Overcome by sorrow, he borrowed brush and inkstone from the waiter and, taking advantage of his drunken inspiration, wrote eight lines on the whitewashed wall: “A champion of justice—that is Lin Chong, a man by nature honest and loyal. His fame has spread throughout the rivers and lakes; in the imperial capital he proved himself a hero. His life drifts sadly like uprooted duckweed; his hopes of glory tumble like windblown thistledown. If fortune favors him in years to come, his might shall awe all lands east of Mount Tai.” He tossed down the brush and called for more wine.

p.src: As he was drinking, the man in the fur coat strode up, seized Lin Chong around the waist, and cried, “What audacity! After committing a monstrous crime in Cangzhou, you dare show yourself here! The authorities are offering a reward of three thousand strings of cash for your capture. What have you to say for yourself?” Lin Chong said, “Who do you think I am?” The man replied, “Are you not Lin Chong, the Panther Head?” “My surname is Zhang,” said Lin Chong. The man laughed. “Do not talk nonsense. You have just written your name on the wall, and the penal brand is on your face. How can you deny it?” Lin Chong said, “Do you truly mean to arrest me?” The man laughed. “What would I arrest you for? Come inside with me, and we shall talk there.” The man released him. Lin Chong followed him to a waterside pavilion at the rear. The man ordered the waiter to light a lamp, exchanged courtesies with Lin Chong, and sat facing him. The man asked, “Just now, elder brother, I heard you repeatedly asking the way to Liangshan Marsh and seeking a boat. That place is a stronghold of outlaws. What business takes you there?” Lin Chong replied, “I will conceal nothing from you. The authorities are now pursuing me relentlessly, and I have nowhere to shelter. I came expressly to join the heroes in that stronghold; that is why I seek passage there.” The man said, “Even so, surely someone has recommended you for admission.” Lin Chong said, “An old friend in Henghai Commandery at Cangzhou recommended me.” “Could it be Chai Jin, the Little Whirlwind?” asked the man. Lin Chong said, “How did you know?” The man replied, “Lord Chai is a close friend of the chief who leads the mountain stronghold, and they often exchange letters.” It turned out that when Wang Lun had failed the civil-service examination, he and Du Qian sought refuge with Chai Jin, who generously kept them at his manor for some time. When they departed, Chai Jin also gave them silver for their traveling expenses; thus they owed him a debt of gratitude. Hearing this, Lin Chong bowed and said, “I failed to recognize a man of stature before me. May I ask your honored name?” The man hurriedly returned the courtesy and said, “I am an agent under Chief Wang. My surname is Zhu and my given name is Gui. I come from Yishui County in Yizhou, and among the rivers and lakes men call me the Dry-Land Crocodile. The stronghold ordered me to set up this inn as a front, specifically to watch the merchants and travelers passing to and fro. Whenever anyone carrying valuables appears, I report it to the stronghold. When a lone traveler comes here without valuables, we let him pass; but if he has wealth, at the least we drug him senseless; at the worst we finish him off at once, slice his lean flesh into dried meat, and render his fat for oil to burn in our lamps. Just now, elder brother, I heard you persistently asking the way to Liangshan Marsh, so I did not dare act against you. Then I saw you write your illustrious name. Men from the eastern capital have told us of your heroism, and I never expected to meet you today. Since you bear Lord Chai’s letter of recommendation and your fame resounds throughout the realm, Chief Wang will surely place great trust in you.” He immediately had fish, meat, platters of food, wine, and delicacies prepared for his guest. The two drank together in the waterside pavilion until midnight. Lin Chong asked, “How can we obtain a boat to cross the water?” Zhu Gui replied, “We have our own boats here, elder brother. Set your mind at ease. Rest here for the night, and at the fifth watch I shall ask you to rise and go with me.” The two then retired separately to rest.

Since you bear Lord Chai’s letter of recommendation and your fame resounds throughout the realm, Chief Wang will surely place great trust in you.”
He immediately had fish, meat, platters of food, wine, and delicacies prepared for his guest.
The two drank together in the waterside pavilion until midnight.
Lin Chong asked, “How can we obtain a boat to cross the water?”
Zhu Gui replied, “We have our own boats here, elder brother. Set your mind at ease.
Rest here for the night, and at the fifth watch I shall ask you to rise and go with me.”
The two then retired separately to rest.

p.src: He slept until the fifth watch, when Zhu Gui came and woke Lin Chong. After Lin had washed, Zhu served him another three or five cups of wine, together with some meat and other food. Dawn had not yet broken. Zhu Gui opened a window of the waterside pavilion, took out a magpie-painted bow, fitted a whistling arrow to it, and shot toward a patch of broken reeds and withered rushes across the inlet. Lin Chong asked, “What does that mean?” Zhu Gui replied, “That is the signal arrow used by the stronghold. A boat will be here shortly.” Before long, several underlings appeared among the reeds across the lake, rowing a swift boat straight to the foot of the waterside pavilion. Zhu Gui then led Lin Chong aboard with his weapons and baggage. The underlings pushed off and rowed into the marsh, making for Golden Sands Beach. As Lin Chong looked upon the eight-hundred-li expanse of the Liangshan Marsh, he saw that it was indeed a place where a man might readily become trapped. This is what he saw:

p.src: The underlings rowed the boat to the shore at Golden Sands Beach, where Zhu Gui and Lin Chong disembarked. An underling shouldered the bundle and carried the weapons, while the two heroes made their way up to the stronghold. The other underlings rowed the boat away into a small inlet. Looking ashore, Lin Chong saw trees so great that a man could barely encircle them with both arms standing on either side, and halfway up the mountain stood the Sever-Gold Pavilion. Rounding another turn, they came upon a great pass. Before it were arrayed spears, sabers, swords, halberds, bows, crossbows, dagger-axes, and lances, while logs and stones for hurling lay ready on every side. An underling went ahead to announce their arrival. When the two passed through the gate, ranks of men and banners lined both sides of the road. Only after passing through two more fortified gates did they reach the entrance to the stronghold. Lin Chong saw lofty mountains on every side and three imposing passes encircling the place completely; In their midst lay a level tract smooth as a mirror, some three to five hundred zhang square; The main gate stood against the mountain pass, with side chambers on either hand.

p.src: Zhu Gui led Lin Chong into the Hall of Righteous Assembly. A hero sat in the central chair: Wang Lun, the “Scholar in White.” In the chair to his left sat Du Qian, the “Sky-Touching One,” and in the chair to his right sat Song Wan, the “Vajra in the Clouds.” Zhu Gui and Lin Chong stepped forward and offered their greetings. Lin Chong stood beside Zhu Gui, who said, “This gentleman was an instructor to the eight hundred thousand Imperial Guards in the Eastern Capital. His surname is Lin, his given name Chong, and his sobriquet is ‘Panther Head.’ He was framed by Grand Marshal Gao and sentenced to exile in Cangzhou, where the army fodder depot was then burned down. Having no other recourse after killing three men, he fled to Squire Chai’s residence, where he was treated with the greatest respect. For that reason, Squire Chai has written this letter expressly to recommend him for admission to our band.”

p.src: Lin Chong took the letter from his breast and handed it over. Wang Lun received it, broke the seal, and read it; then he invited Lin Chong to sit in the fourth chair, while Zhu Gui took the fifth. He ordered the underlings to bring wine, and after three rounds of cups asked courteously whether Squire Chai had lately been in good health. Lin Chong replied, “Every day he hunts in the countryside for pleasure.” After Wang Lun had asked him a few more questions, a thought suddenly struck him: “I am merely a scholar who failed the examinations. Driven by resentment, I came here with Du Qian and turned outlaw; Later Song Wan joined us, and together we gathered all these men and followers. I possess no great abilities, and Du Qian and Song Wan are only mediocre fighters. Now, if we admit this man, an instructor of the Imperial Guards in the capital, he is certain to be highly skilled in arms. If he should see through the limits of our abilities, he is bound to overpower us. How could we withstand him? Better to invent some pretext, refuse him, and send him down the mountain, thereby averting future trouble. It would indeed be an affront to Chai Jin and would mean forgetting his past kindness, but I cannot afford to heed him now.” Indeed:

p.src: Wang Lun at once ordered the underlings to prepare food and wine and lay out a banquet. He invited Lin Chong to take his seat, and all the heroes drank together. As the feast drew to its close, Wang Lun had an underling bring out a tray bearing fifty taels of silver and two bolts of ramie silk. Wang Lun rose and said, “His Excellency Chai recommended that you, Instructor, join our humble stronghold. Unfortunately, our little refuge is short of provisions, its buildings are in poor repair, and its manpower is scant. I fear we would fail you in days to come, which would reflect badly upon us. Here is a trifling gift; I beg you to accept it with a smile. Seek some greater stronghold where you may find shelter and rest your horse, and please do not take offense.” Lin Chong said, “Allow me to answer you, chiefs. This humble man has ‘traveled a thousand li to offer his name and ten thousand to find a lord.’ Relying upon His Excellency Chai’s good offices, I came directly to this great stronghold to join you. Though I possess little talent, I beg you to take me in. I shall advance even unto death, without flattery or deceit. To be accepted would be the greatest fortune of my life. I did not come for a gift of silver; I beg you chiefs to understand this.” Wang Lun said, “This is but a small place. How could we possibly accommodate you? Do not blame me, do not blame me.” Seeing this, Zhu Gui remonstrated, “Elder brother, please forgive your younger brother for speaking too freely. Though provisions in the stronghold are scarce, we can borrow some from villages nearby or towns farther away. The hills and marsh abound in timber; even if we wished to build a thousand rooms, it would present no difficulty. This man was earnestly recommended by His Excellency Chai. How can we send him elsewhere? Besides, His Excellency Chai has always shown kindness to our mountain. If he later learns that we refused this man, it will reflect badly upon us. This is also a man of ability, and he will surely exert himself on our behalf.” Du Qian said, “What difference can one more man make to the stronghold? If you refuse to receive him, elder brother, His Excellency Chai will blame us when he learns of it, and we shall plainly appear ungrateful and faithless. We have so often benefited from him in the past. Now that he recommends one man to us, how can we reject him so and send him away?” Song Wan also urged him, “For His Excellency Chai’s sake, it would be well to let him remain here as a chief. Otherwise we shall show ourselves devoid of honor and become a laughingstock among the gallant men of the rivers and lakes.” Wang Lun said, “Brothers, you do not understand. Though he committed a monstrous crime in Cangzhou and has now come up the mountain, we do not know what lies in his heart. What are we to do if he has come to spy out our true circumstances?” Lin Chong said, “This humble man is under sentence of death and has therefore come to join your band. Why do you suspect me?” Wang Lun said, “If that is so, and you sincerely wish to join us, bring me a pledge of admission.” Lin Chong promptly replied, “I know a few characters. Bring me paper and brush, and I shall write it at once.” Zhu Gui laughed. “You are mistaken, Instructor. Whenever a gallant man joins our band, he must present a pledge of admission: you are to go down the mountain, kill someone, and offer up his head. Then he will harbor no suspicions. That is what we call a pledge of admission.” Lin Chong said, “That is not difficult. I shall go down the mountain and wait. My only fear is that no one will pass by.” Wang Lun said, “I give you three days. If you bring a pledge of admission within three days, I shall allow you to join us. If you have none after three days, you must not blame me.” Lin Chong agreed and returned to his room for the night, oppressed by unending gloom. Indeed:

p.src: Toward evening, Lin Chong gathered his weapons and baggage, and an underling led him to a guest room, where he spent the night. He rose early the next morning, ate some food and drank tea, girded on his sword, and took up his long-handled broadsword. An underling guided him down the mountain and ferried him across the water, and there he waited on a secluded path for travelers to pass. From morning until dusk he waited the whole day, but not a single solitary traveler passed. Deeply dejected, Lin Chong crossed back with the underling and returned to the stronghold. Wang Lun asked, “Where is your pledge of admission?” Lin Chong replied, “Not a single traveler passed today, so I was unable to obtain one.” Wang Lun said, “If you still have no pledge tomorrow, it will be difficult for you to remain here.” Lin Chong dared make no reply. Displeased at heart, he returned to his room, asked for some food, ate, and passed another night there.

p.src: Early the next morning, he rose, ate breakfast with the underling, took up his long-handled broadsword, and again descended the mountain. The underling said, “Today let us go and wait on the southern mountain road.” The two concealed themselves in the woods and waited, but not one traveler passed. They lay in wait until noon, when a company of some three hundred travelers came by in a body. Lin Chong dared not attack them and watched them pass. They waited a while longer. Dusk was drawing near, yet still not a single traveler appeared. Lin Chong said to the underling, “What wretched luck I have! I have waited two days without seeing a single lone traveler pass. What am I to do?” The underling said, “Take heart, elder brother. You still have one day left tomorrow. I will go with you to wait on the eastern mountain road.” That evening they went back up the mountain as before. Wang Lun said, “How did you fare with your pledge of admission today?” Lin Chong dared not answer and merely heaved a sigh. Wang Lun laughed. “I suppose you failed again today. I gave you a limit of three days, and two have now passed. If you still have nothing tomorrow, there will be no need for us to meet again. You must trouble yourself to go down the mountain and seek refuge elsewhere.”

p.src: That night Lin Chong raised his face to heaven and sighed deeply. “Who would have thought that today I should be framed by that villain Gao Qiu and reduced to wandering here, only to find that even Heaven and Earth have no place for me? How bitterly ill-fated and untimely my lot is!” After another night had passed, he rose at daybreak, asked for some food and ate it, then tied up his bundle and left it in the room. He girded on his sword, took up his long-handled broadsword, and again descended the mountain with the underling. They crossed the water and made for the eastern mountain road. Lin Chong said, “If I still cannot obtain a pledge of admission today, I shall have no choice but to seek a livelihood elsewhere.” The two reached the woods along the eastern road below the mountain and concealed themselves to wait. The sun climbed toward noon, but still not a single person came.

p.src: It was just then that the last snow cleared and the sun shone brightly. Lin Chong, carrying his cudgel-sword, said to the young bandit, “It plainly seems that nothing will come of this after all. We had better leave while it is still early. Before night falls, we shall fetch our baggage and seek shelter elsewhere.” The young fellow pointed and said, “All is well! Is that not someone coming over there?” Lin Chong looked and cried, “Thank heaven!” He saw a man in the distance who had spotted them from below the mountain slope and was coming their way. When the man drew nearer, Lin Chong flourished his cudgel-sword and suddenly sprang out. At the sight of Lin Chong, the fellow cried, “Aiya!” He dropped his carrying pole, turned, and fled. Lin Chong gave chase, but how could he catch him? The fellow slipped around the mountain slope and vanished. Lin Chong said, “See how wretched my fate is! I have been here three days and had only just managed to wait until someone came, yet I let him escape.” The young bandit said, “Though you did not manage to kill the man, this load of valuables should suffice.” Lin Chong said, “Carry it up the mountain first. I shall wait a little longer.” The young bandit shouldered the load and carried it out of the woods.
